checks.claim: BT1 abstract covariance and seen Cameron geometry: Cov_delta=sqrt(delta)Mean_delta, ker Cov=Hseen^perp, ||Cov h||_CM=||P_seen h||, Ball_CM=Cov(Ball_Hraw(1))=sqrt(delta)Mean_delta(Ball(1)), Tube_r=A+(r/sqrt(delta))Ball_CM
checks.reason: From ell(X)=W(k_ell) and (1) we get ell(Cov h)=<k_ell,h>, so the kernel is exactly Hseen^perp. P_seen maps the closed raw unit ball onto the closed Hseen unit ball, and Cov kills the orthogonal part, so the raw-ball image is exactly the closed CM unit ball. The scaling Mean_delta(Ball(r))=(r/sqrt(delta))Ball_CM then follows from Cov=sqrt(delta)Mean. This is exact geometry, not an embedding bound, and no constant enters the action.

checks.claim: Compact, closed raw-ball image via Hilbert weak compactness; closed base plus compact image is closed
checks.reason: Bounded sequences in separable Hilbert space have weakly convergent subsequences (diagonal coordinates), and the norm bound passes to the limit by Fatou. Bounded operators are weak-weak continuous, so every norm limit point of compact images equals Mean h. The whole subsequence therefore converges, which gives a sequentially compact and hence compact and closed image. For a closed set plus a compact set, extract a convergent compact component, so A_delta+K is closed and Borel. No uniform-R or uniform-delta compactness is used.
